identity.title: Hypoglycemia history: insulin/sulfonylurea use, missed meals, adrenergic or neuroglycopenic symptoms

technique.how: Ask about insulin or sulfonylurea use (agent, dose, timing of last dose, recent change), missed meals, unusual exertion, alcohol, renal/hepatic impairment, and prior severe hypoglycemia or unawareness. Elicit adrenergic (sweating, tremor, palpitations, hunger) and neuroglycopenic (confusion, behaviour change, focal deficit, seizure) symptoms and their relief by carbohydrate.
technique.prerequisites: Obtain a fingerstick glucose at the time of symptoms whenever possible; collateral history from witnesses for confusion or loss of consciousness.
technique.contraindications: None; history-taking must never delay a bedside glucose measurement in any patient with altered mental state.

interpretation.positive_finding: Insulin or secretagogue exposure plus a missed meal, alcohol, renal impairment or a dose change, with adrenergic/neuroglycopenic symptoms relieved by carbohydrate, makes hypoglycemia the leading explanation and warrants documented low glucose (Whipple's triad).
interpretation.negative_finding: No insulin/secretagogue exposure and no relation of symptoms to fasting or food makes drug-induced hypoglycemia unlikely, but a measured glucose is still required in altered mental status.
interpretation.pitfalls: Beta-blockers, autonomic neuropathy and recurrent hypoglycemia blunt adrenergic warning symptoms (hypoglycemia unawareness); sulfonylurea hypoglycemia recurs for 24-72 h and can present as focal deficit mimicking stroke. Symptoms alone are nonspecific and overlap with anxiety and arrhythmia.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: measure/treat glucose now and observe for recurrence with secretagogues or long-acting insulin; negative: keep vasovagal, arrhythmic and neurological causes in play.

sources.citation: Cryer PE, Axelrod L, Grossman AB, Heller SR, et al. Evaluation and management of adult hypoglycemic disorders: an Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2009.
Hepburn DA, Deary IJ, Frier BM, Patrick AW, et al. Symptoms of acute insulin-induced hypoglycemia in humans with and without IDDM. Factor-analysis approach. Diabetes Care. 1991.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Never rely on symptom history instead of a point-of-care glucose in any patient with altered mental status, seizure or focal deficit.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Sulfonylurea or long-acting insulin overdose, recurrent hypoglycemia despite feeding, or hypoglycemia in a non-diabetic patient needs admission and further evaluation (sepsis, adrenal or hepatic failure, insulinoma, factitious use).
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No inter-observer data; symptom recall is unreliable in patients with hypoglycemia unawareness.

extraction_notes: Searched 'hypoglycemia symptoms sensitivity specificity awareness prospective' (no diagnostic-accuracy study of the history for hypoglycemia as a cause of syncope/AMS was found; hits were unrelated). Hepburn 1991 characterises symptom clusters by factor analysis in 55 subjects during induced hypoglycemia (Abstract) but reports no sensitivity/specificity, so no estimate is entered. The Endocrine Society guideline (Cryer 2009) anchors the diagnostic approach (Whipple's triad, drug review, risk factors) as consensus. Status not_quantified; the record carries no numbers. Author names copied from tools/pubmed.py fetch output (first four listed, then et al.).
